text: A row of lamps on a shelf, thirty of them, each with a number stamped on.
A banksman gives out the lamps at the shaft head and takes them back,
and the numbers are how he knows whether everybody came up.
The kitchen. One cup out. One chair pulled out.
A bed made up in the front room, on the ground floor, near the door.
The stairs to the proper bedroom have a coat hung over the rail
and have not been used in a while.
A framed lamp check, number 12, mounted on its own.
The card under it gives a date and a name and nothing else.
Everyone in Stonewake over forty knows the date.
